children: Strong server sales and a huge buyback program support the rally. The next test is whether earnings can keep pace with Nvidia’s growing market value.
A record close puts $6 trillion within reach
Nvidia

climbed 2.1% to $238.90 on Monday, setting a record closing price. Shares reached $240.10 during the session, leaving the close roughly 0.5% below that intraday peak. The advance helped lift the Nasdaq Composite to
The chipmaker’s market capitalization now stands at

, about $230 billion short of $6 trillion. With roughly 24.15 billion shares outstanding, that milestone would require a price around $248.45, assuming the share count stays unchanged — another 4% higher.

Shares are up 28% this year. Nvidia’s size also makes the move consequential beyond semiconductor portfolios: its heavy weighting in major US indexes means a strong session can support the headline benchmarks even when gains elsewhere are less convincing.
Server demand provides fresh evidence
Foxconn, Nvidia’s biggest server manufacturer, reported 47% growth in third-quarter revenue to $95.4 billion, beating forecasts. Strong AI demand largely drove that increase.
Nvidia’s own latest results showed quarterly revenue rising 106% to $96.2 billion. Data-center sales increased 117% to $89 billion, accounting for more than 92% of total revenue.
That concentration explains why spending on AI infrastructure remains the most important driver of its earnings outlook. Shareholder returns provide another support.

Nvidia authorized an additional $150 billion of buybacks on September 28, taking its remaining program to $235 billion, expected to be executed through fiscal 2028. Repurchases can lift earnings per share by reducing the share count.
The milestone still needs earnings support

Despite its enormous market value, Nvidia trades at around 20 times forecast earnings, compared with around 30 times trailing earnings. The difference reflects expectations for substantial profit growth.
Traders should recognize the dependency: weaker earnings forecasts would make today’s valuation look more demanding without any increase in the share price.
Management’s next-quarter revenue guidance is $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, with gross margins around 74%. Interestingly, that outlook assumes no data-center compute revenue from China.
On the chart, $240.10 is the immediate reference high, followed by the roughly 248-249 area associated with a $6 trillion price tag.
That second level is milestone arithmetic, not established technical resistance. A sustained move beyond Monday’s high could provide stronger evidence of momentum than a brief intraday spike.
